text: Interval training is a series of high-intensity, short duration exercises or drills followed by a period of rest. The ratio of this work-to-rest interval is typically 1-to-10 (which is applicable to most power-based sports). This means if the drill lasts 5 s, the athlete should then be given 50 s to recover before performing another drill. Rather than having all athletes in a single group run at the same time, rest cycles can be easily built into drills by dividing the athletes into two smaller groups. This allows one group to perform the drill while the other rests.
